page_title: DiskPilot: your Mac is full. Find out why.

sources.entry: DiskPilot - Free, open-source storage analyzer for developers that explains each folder (Docker, node_modules, Xcode DerivedData, AI tool caches), marks what is safe to delete and moves everything to the Trash first. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/Devanshgoel-123/diskpilot) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.name: DiskPilot
summary.one_liner: DiskPilot is a free, open-source macOS storage analyzer for developers that explains what Docker, Xcode, node_modules and AI tools left on disk and cleans it up only after review, moving items to the Trash first.
keywords: find what is using my mac storage
use_cases: Find out why a developer's Mac storage is full
Clean up Docker images, containers and volumes safely
Remove stale Xcode DerivedData and simulator data
Delete node_modules and build output from old projects
Reclaim space from AI coding tool and local model caches
summary.what_it_does: DiskPilot scans the home folder read-only and sizes what is taking up space, then names each folder by tool, project and version using a rule-based classifier that shows a confidence level and a plain-language explanation. It covers developer data such as Docker, Xcode DerivedData, node_modules, package manager caches, Rust, Python, editor workspace storage and AI tool caches. Each item gets a tier: Likely safe, Review first or Keep, and anything it does not understand is shown as Unknown and never suggested. Cleanup is a reviewed plan: you confirm exact paths, items move to the Trash, each path is re-checked just before moving, and every action is recorded in History. The page also describes an optional assistant that uses your own API key from Anthropic, OpenAI or OpenRouter, and a sorted view of your files by type.
notable: Explains each folder with a rule, confidence level and reason, not just sizes
Trash first: items are recoverable until the Trash is emptied, and every Docker command is shown before it runs
Docker volumes are removed only when selected and confirmed by typing the container name
MIT licensed, signed and notarized by Apple, with signed build attestations
caveats: macOS only; Windows support is planned but not yet available
Optional AI assistant needs the user's own API key from a third-party provider
